bull_bear.body:
- Early entry (2011) into inverter-duty transformers ahead of India's renewable build-out produced a large installed base (14 GW+ of solar and wind installations supported) and a field-performance record generating continued inquiry flow
- In-house NABL-accredited testing laboratory shortens the type-testing loop, the rate-limiting step in qualifying products at 245 kV, supporting a credible timeline into the Extra High Voltage segment where competition is thinner
- Core processes performed in-house (coil winding, tank fabrication, high-voltage testing, oil filtration/processing) reduce dependence on external component lead times, which the IEA identifies as the binding global industry constraint
- Low customer concentration - CRISIL's March 2026 rating rationale notes no single customer accounts for more than 15-20% of revenue
- Approximately 80% of business comes from repeat customers (per Managing Director's message)
- Product failure rate below 0.15%
- Among the first Indian manufacturers to receive a BIS licence for ester-filled distribution transformers, positioning it in the fire-safety-driven urban substation and data-centre segment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body: - Workforce churn / retention — As on 31 March 2026 the Company employed 617 personnel (537 permanent, 80 contractual); during the year 193 new employees were appointed while 100 resigned, indicating meaningful hiring and attrition activity in a technically skilled manufacturing workforce that management must continually replenish and train (health/safety and skill-development programmes were run across departments during the year).

business.body: Danish Power designs, manufactures and supplies transformers (oil and dry-type power and distribution transformers, inverter-duty and wind turbine generator transformers, traction transformers, pad-mounted and special application transformers, dry-type cast resin transformers, compact and skid-mounted substations), together with control relay panels and substation automation systems, to the renewable energy, power transmission and distribution, and industrial utility segments in India and internationally. Power transformers are manufactured up to the 245 kV class, and control relay panels/substation automation systems up to the 400 kV class. Renewable energy contributes close to 60% of revenues, with transformers cumulatively supporting over 14 GW of solar and wind installations worldwide.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Transformers:** Oil and dry-type power transformers, Oil and dry-type distribution transformers, Inverter-duty transformers, Wind turbine generator transformers, Traction transformers, Pad-mounted and special application transformers, Dry-type cast resin transformers, Compact and skid-mounted substations
- **Control & Automation:** Control relay panels, Substation automation systems

- Early entry (2011) into inverter-duty transformers ahead of India's renewable build-out produced a large installed base (14 GW+ of solar and wind installations supported) and a field-performance record generating continued inquiry flow
- In-house NABL-accredited testing laboratory shortens the type-testing loop, the rate-limiting step in qualifying products at 245 kV, supporting a credible timeline into the Extra High Voltage segment where competition is thinner
- Core processes performed in-house (coil winding, tank fabrication, high-voltage testing, oil filtration/processing) reduce dependence on external component lead times, which the IEA identifies as the binding global industry constraint
- Low customer concentration - CRISIL's March 2026 rating rationale notes no single customer accounts for more than 15-20% of revenue

- Product failure rate below 0.15%
- Among the first Indian manufacturers to receive a BIS licence for ester-filled distribution transformers, positioning it in the fire-safety-driven urban substation and data-centre segment
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Progressively utilise expanded manufacturing capacity and build greater scale in power transformers and higher-voltage segments
- Increase export contribution and pursue opportunities across renewable energy, BESS and emerging applications such as data centres
- Backward integration of sheet metal fabrication, planned to go live in FY 2026-27
- Prioritise profitable growth over revenue at any cost, with customer selection, execution quality and commercial discipline shaping order acquisition (selective, margin-conscious approach)
- Deepen capabilities in digital substation technologies, intelligent monitoring, protection and control solutions, and SCADA integration
- Strengthen presence in higher-voltage transformer segments and expand reach across domestic and international markets
- Invest in technical training, skill development, leadership capabilities and talent pipeline to support scaling operations
- Introduce an Employee Stock Option Scheme (Board-approved, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals) to strengthen employee participation and align interests with shareholders
- Dividend is recommended by the Board based on the Company's financial performance, profitability and available distributable surplus per the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, and is subject to shareholder approval by Ordinary Resolution at the Annual General Meeting; for FY2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend of 20% (Rs 2 per equity share of Rs 10 face value) aggregating Rs 3,93,83,220, put before the 40th AGM for declaration and payment.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company executed a two-phase capacity expansion during FY2025-26, funded through a combination of IPO proceeds and internal accruals. Phase 1 (approx. 2,500 MVA) became operational at the Company's owned facility at Plot No. DTA-02-08, DTA Phase-II, Mahindra World City, Jaipur (the Directors' Report states this happened in October 2025; the Corporate Overview / Manufacturing Excellence sections state commissioning in September 2025). Phase 2 (approx. 3,000 MVA) was completed during FY2025-26 with commercial operations commencing in January 2026, at a facility on land owned by Evernest Shelter Private Limited (a related party / wholly owned subsidiary), on plots contiguous to the Company's existing facility. Together the two phases took installed annual transformer manufacturing capacity from approximately 4,700 MVA to over 11,000 MVA (an addition described elsewhere as 5,500+ MVA), and extended manufacturing capability to power transformers up to 100 MVA in the 245 kV class, enabling entry into the Extra High Voltage segment. The Company manufactures at two facilities in Jaipur - Sitapura Industrial Area and Mahindra World City - with a combined manufacturing area of over 3,00,000 sq. ft. following the expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Renewable energy expansion in India driving large-scale investment in solar and wind projects, increasing demand for specialised transformers for generation, evacuation and grid integration
- Grid modernisation and sustained transmission & distribution infrastructure investment increasing demand for higher-capacity, technologically advanced transformer solutions
- Rapid deployment of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) reshaping the power landscape by enabling grid stability and renewable integration
- Rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and expansion of data centres increasing demand for reliable, energy-efficient electrical infrastructure
- Beyond domestic demand, the global replacement cycle for ageing power infrastructure is creating a parallel demand avenue, including for exports
- Demand emerging from the Thermal Power segment, with NTPC approval and NTPC's stated growth plans cited as a driver
- Management states it has consistently prioritised profitable growth over pursuing revenue at any cost, with product mix, operating efficiency, capital deployment and margins as ongoing areas of focus
- Order book exceeding Rs 600 crore, reflecting sustained demand across Power, Distribution and Renewable Energy segments
- Enquiry pipeline worth over Rs 1,000 crore
- Exports currently account for Rs 115 crore of the order book, cited as a base for further international expansion
